THESE APPEALS HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT AND COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY THROUGH VIDEO CONFEENCING AT KALABURAGI, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

These two appeals by the owner and rider of the offending vehicle are directed against the common NC: 2023:KHC:46988 judgment and award dated 07.10.2015 in MVC No.246/2010 & 247/2010 passed by the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Chamarajanagar, whereby the liability was fastened against the appellants herein.

2. The facts in nutshell are as below:
In both these claim petitions, the claimants contended that on 29.05.2010 at about 8.30 a.m., on Santhemarahalli, T.N.Pura road, when the petitioner M.P.Shankara was proceeding on his Motorcycle along with pillion rider Mahesh, (the claimant in connected case) took turn towards his land, respondent No.2- B.G.Nandeesh who was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-10-K-6298 came in rash and negligent Mahesha vs Mahesha on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34650866/
3 manner from hind side and dashed against the motorcycle of the claimants and as a result, they fell down and sustained injuries.

Both the claimants/petitioners were taken to Sri Shivarathri Rajendra Hospital, Pachappa Circle, Chamarajanagar and after first aid, it was found that claimant M.P.Shankara has NC: 2023:KHC:46988 sustained fractures and therefore, he was taken to Mahadeshwara Nursing home on 03.06.2010 and surgeries had to be performed.
He was discharged from the hospital on 05.06.2010.

The petitioner M.P.Shankara contended that he was doing contract work and was constructing the Government buildings and he was also doing agriculture and therefore, he is entitled for the compensation from the rider, owner and insurer of the offending motorcycle.

The claimant in MVC No.246/2010 contended that he was a coolie and was working as a loader in a Tractor and he also sustained injuries and therefore, he is also entitled for the compensation from the rider, owner and insurer of the offending motorcycle.
3. Respondent No.1-
Mahesh

S / o. Sannasetty appeared and filed objections stating that the petitions are not maintainable and that there was no such negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle i.e., B.G.Nandeesh and denied the amount spent by the petitioners for their treatment and termed the NC: 2023:KHC:46988 compensation claimed as highly excessive and exorbitant.
He contended that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner M.P.Shankara who drove his motorcycle in negligent manner and fell down.

However, he has contended that his vehicle was insured with respondent No.3-Insurance Company and the rider was having a valid driving licence and as such, the liability has to be fastened upon the respondent No.3-insurer.

4. Respondent No.2, rider B.G.Nandeesh appeared and filed objection stating that the petition is not maintainable and he denied the age, avocation etc., of the petitioners and also contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the claimant M.P.Shankara and therefore, there was no such negligence on his part.

5. Respondent No.3- Insurance Company also resisted the claim petitions contending that the petitions are not maintainable either in law or on fact and denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioners.

It contended that the rider of the motorcycle is shown as NC: 2023:KHC:46988 Mahesh S/o Shivananjappa as per the complaint at the FIR, but subsequently, charge sheet was laid against B.G.Nandeesh as a rider and it shows that respondents No.1 and 2 colluded with each other and implicated the said B.G.Nandeesh as a rider.
It is contended that there is also delay in filing the complaint and therefore, the petitions are liable to be dismissed as against the insurer.
6. On the basis of the above contentions, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and both the petitions were clubbed as they were arising out of the same accident.
The petitioners examined three witnesses as PW1 to PW3 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P26.
The petitions were disposed of by the Tribunal on 02.01.2012 awarding compensation to the petitioners, fastening the liability on respondent No.3-insurance company.

The claimants as well as the insurer had preferred MFA No.10082/2012, MFA No.3432/2012 and MFA No.3433/2012 before this Court and those appeals were disposed of remanding the matter to the Tribunal with a direction to re-determine the NC:
2023:KHC:46988 compensation afresh and to pass appropriate orders in accordance with law after Mahesha vs Mahesha on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34650866/
4 affording opportunity to both the parties.

Accordingly, after the remand the Tribunal framed an additional issue as below:
1.
Whether respondent No.1 proves that driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and hence respondent No.3 is liable to pay compensation?

7. Thus the issues framed by the Tribunal in both these claim petitions are as below which are identical in nature:
1.

Whether the respective petitioners prove that they sustained injuries in the motor vehicle accident that took place on 29.05.2010 at about 8.30 a.m, on Mysore-Santhemaralli main road near the garden house of petitioner (Shankara)
while negotiating a turn towards his land in his motorcycle, due to rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-10/K-6298 by its rider?
2.
Whether the respective petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. To what order or award?
NC: 2023:KHC:46988
Similar issues were framed in the connected case also.
8. Thereafter, opportunities were given to both the sides and respondent No.3-insurance company examined RW2 Mahesh S/o Shivananjappa.

After examining the evidence on record and hearing both the sides, the Tribunal answered issue No.1 in the affirmative, issue No.2 partly in affirmative and additional issue No.1 in the negative and fastened the liability on respondents No.1 and 2 in both the petitions directing them to pay the compensation of Rs.1,81,300/-in MVC No.246/2010 and a sum of Rs.80,000/- in MVC No.247/2010.
9.

Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, respondents No.1 and 2, who were fastened with the liability to pay the compensation to both the petitioners, have approached this Court in these appeals.

10. In both the appeals, the appellants who are the owner and rider of the offending motorcycle contended that the Tribunal has erroneously fastened the liability on them and absolved the liability against the insurer.
They - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 contend that the appreciation of the evidence by the Tribunal is not proper and correct and therefore, the impugned judgment and award is not sustainable under law.
They specifically contended that the appreciation of the evidence of RW2 is perverse.

Mahesha vs Mahesha on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34650866/
5 11.
On being issued with the notices, the claimants and the Insurance Company have appeared through their counsel in both the appeals.
The Tribunal records have been secured and the arguments by both the sides are heard.

12. The only point that arises for consideration in these appeals are: whether the Tribunal erred in appreciating the evidence on record and in fastening the liability on the owner and rider of the offending motorcycle No.KA-10/K-6298?
13. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that the evidence of RW2 is not an admission and the Tribunal erred in appreciating the evidence of RW2.

He submits that the claimants have - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 stated in their evidence that the offending vehicle was driven by appellant No.2-Nandeesh and the charge sheet was also filed against appellant No.2.
Therefore, RW2 who was shown to be the rider of the offending motorcycle in the FIR, was in no way concerned to the case.

It is contended that when there is charge sheet against appellant No.2 filed by the investigating officer,
it is not necessary to clarify the stand by these appellants.
He contends that the claims of the claimants itself is fraudulent and fraud and justice do not dwell together.
It is contended that none had suggested RW2 that he was the rider and the deposition of RW2 has been wrongly understood by the Tribunal and it came to a wrong conclusion.
Therefore, he contends that the Tribunal erred in fastening the liability on the appellants/ respondent No.1 and 2 before the Tribunal.

14. In support of his contention, learned counsel for the appellant has relied on the decision in the case of S.P Chengalvaraya Naidu (dead) by LRs V/s - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 Jagannath, reported in (1994) 1 SCC 1 and in the case of Ram Preeti Yadav V/s U.P. Board of High School and Intermediate Education and Others, reported in (2003) 8 SCC 311 where in it was held that fraud and justice do not dwell together.
15.

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.3-Insurance Company contended that the evidence of RW2 is clear and he has deposed that he was rider of the offending motorcycle.

He contends that the FIR which was filed after 30 days of the accident clearly mention that the motorcycle was ridden by RW2 and the Tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion that in order to make unlawful gain, the petitioners gave a statement at a subsequent stage that the vehicle was ridden by B.G.Nandeesh but not RW2.
This clearly shows that such a manipulation was done only with an intention of making unlawful gain and for fastening the liability on the Insurance Company.

He contends that the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence of RW2 and has come - 13 - Mahesha vs Mahesha on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34650866/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:46988 to the conclusion that the petitions as against the insurer is liable to be dismissed.
16. There were no arguments on the part of the claimants.
17. The perusal of the Tribunal records would show that earlier, RW2 was shown to be the rider in the cause title.
Later an amendment came to be brought to the petitions stating that Mahesh S/o Sannasetty was the owner of the offending motorcycle.
It can also be seen that the FIR and complaint, which are produced at Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 show that the claimant M.P.Shankara had lodged the complaint on 29.06.2010.

In the said complaint, it was stated that on 29.05.2010 at about 8.30 a.m., when he and the pillion rider Mahesh S/o Ningappa were going on their motorcycle and were to take turn towards their land, the new motorcycle belonging to Mahesh S/o Shivananjappa was driven by him in high speed and in negligent manner and dashed against their motorcycle resulting in the complainant and the pillion rider falling down and sustaining injuries.

It was stated - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 that it was a new vehicle and the elders of the village represented that since it was a new vehicle, they would settle the matter and therefore, he did not lodged any complaint.
He also stated that one Nagaraju and Madan Kumar had seen the accident and they had shifted the injured to the hospital.
The said complaint was registered by the police and investigation was launched.

18. Thereafter, it appears that the petitioner M.P.Shankar gave further statement before the Investigating Officer and informed that in a hurry he had stated that the name of the rider as Mahesh s/o Shivananjappa but the rider was one B.G.Nandeesh.
He had also stated that he did not have full consciousness at the time of the accident and therefore, he had mentioned the name of the rider of the motorcycle wrongly.
Obviously, the said statement which is produced at Ex.P4 is not dated and in all probability it is subsequent to the filing of the complaint on 29.06.2010.

On the basis of the said statement, the Investigating Officer has proceeded with the investigation and ultimately, filed charge sheet against the said B.G.Nandeesh as per Ex.P21.
20.

In the evidence, PW1 M.P.Shankar has stated before the Tribunal that immediately after the accident he was taken to Sri Shivarathri Rajendra Hospital, Chamarajanagar, and on the same day he had been discharged from the hospital.
Thereafter, he took treatment as an outpatient at the Primary Health Centre and at that time, he took the X-ray and found that there were fracture injuries.
Thereafter, he went to Mahadeshwara Nursing Home on 03.06.2010.
He was discharged from Mahadeshwara Nursing Home after the surgery on 05.06.2010 and then, continued the treatment at the Primary Health Centre at Santhemarahalli.

In the cross-examination dated Mahesha vs Mahesha on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34650866/
7 11.07.2011, he states that respondent No.1 was riding the offending motorcycle.

He does not mention that respondent No.2, i.e.,
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 B.G.Nandeesh, was riding the motorcycle.
It is also elicited in the cross-examination that after lodging the complaint, he did not visited the Police Station.
Thus, in examination- in-chief, PW.1 states that it was respondent No.1 who was riding the motorcycle, but in fact, it was respondent No.2- B.G.Nandeesh as per the chargesheet.

In his further statement, after the remand of the matter to the Tribunal, in his affidavit, he stated that while he was taking treatment, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were called for negotiation and they did not come forward and therefore, there is delay in filing the complaint.
21. PW.2 deposed in similar fashion and PW.3 have also given similar evidence.
22. From the above evidence, it is clear that there is a delay of 30 days in filing the complaint.

PW.1 was discharged from the hospital on 05.06.2010 and therefore, it is difficult to accept the contention of the petitioner that he was unconscious after the accident and in a hurry; he did not mention the name of the rider of the motorcycle in - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 a proper way.

The testimony of PW.1-M.P.Shankar shows that on the date of the accident itself, he was discharged from the hospital and later, he came to know that he had sustained the fracture injuries and therefore, he was admitted to the hospital, where he was treated by PW.3- Dr.Krishna Prasad.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that on 05.06.2010,
he was unconscious or he was unable to give a statement.
However, the complaint was lodged after about one month i.e., on 29.06.2010.
The said complaint as per Ex.P2 does not mention that the motorcycle was driven by the said B.G.Nandeesh.
Hence, the contention that the petitioners did not know the name of the rider of the motorcycle to be B.G.Nandeesh cannot be accepted.
23. The another important aspect to be noted is that the evidence of PW.1 is self contradictory.
The explanation for delay is stated to be that the vehicle was new and therefore the elders of the village had assured that there would be a settlement.
The vehicle was - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 registered on 20.10.2009 and the insurance policy was issued much prior to it i.e., on 25.09.2009.
Therefore, the explanation for delay that it was a new vehicle and as such, the elders of the village tried for a settlement is not acceptable.
The vehicle was registered more than eight months prior to the accident.

24. The third aspect to be noted is regarding the testimony of RW.2. RW.2-Mahesh s/o Shivananjappa (who was initially arrayed as R-1) states as below:

25. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants contend that the above evidence of RW.2 is not properly appreciated by the Tribunal.
Obviously, it cannot be said that the commas have been typed as full stops and a wrong interpretation is inferred by the Tribunal.
The deposition was recorded in Kannada and there is no room for any wrong interpretation.
Therefore, the testimony of RW.2 clearly depict that he was the rider and he did not possess a driving licence.

Under these circumstances, the Tribunal in paragraph Nos.31 and 32 has rightly come to the conclusion that the evidence of RW.2 categorically shows that he was the rider but he was not possessing the - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 valid driving license.
It also noticed that RW.2 was not at all cross-examined by the learned counsel for the petitioners or respondent No.1, who is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The version of RW.2 has remained unchallenged.
Therefore, when there is no challenge to the testimony of RW.2, the Tribunal is justified in drawing the conclusion that the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.

Even if we hold that the vehicle owned by respondent No.1 was involved in the accident, the rider of the motorcycle, who was none else than RW.2, was not possessing a valid driving licence and therefore, respondent No.3-Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

When respondent No.1- owner and respondent No.2-Nandeesh have admitted that there was an accident involving the motorcycle belonging to respondent No.1, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on them.

26. In that view of the matter, the factual matrix of the case clearly shows that there was a false implication Mahesha vs Mahesha on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34650866/
9 - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 and breach of conditions of policy.
Therefore, the appeals are devoid of merits.

Hence the following:
ORDER
Both the Appeals are dismissed with costs.
The amount in deposit in both the appeals shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.

Respondent No.2, rider B.G.Nandeesh appeared and filed objection stating that the petition is not maintainable and he denied the age, avocation etc., of the petitioners and also contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the claimant M.P.Shankara and therefore, there was no such negligence on his part.
5. Respondent No.3- Insurance Company also resisted the claim petitions contending that the petitions are not maintainable either in law or on fact and denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioners.
It contended that the rider of the motorcycle is shown as NC: 2023:KHC:46988 Mahesh S/o Shivananjappa as per the complaint at the FIR, but subsequently, charge sheet was laid against B.G.Nandeesh as a rider and it shows that respondents No.1 and 2 colluded with each other and implicated the said B.G.Nandeesh as a rider.
10. In both the appeals, the appellants who are the owner and rider of the offending motorcycle contended that the Tribunal has erroneously fastened the liability on them and absolved the liability against the insurer.
Therefore, he contends that the Tribunal erred in fastening the liability on the appellants/ respondent No.1 and 2 before the Tribunal.
14. In support of his contention, learned counsel for the appellant has relied on the decision in the case of S.P Chengalvaraya Naidu (dead) by LRs V/s - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:46988 Jagannath, reported in (1994) 1 SCC 1 and in the case of Ram Preeti Yadav V/s U.P. Board of High School and Intermediate Education and Others, reported in (2003) 8 SCC 311 where in it was held that fraud and justice do not dwell together.
15.
This clearly shows that such a manipulation was done only with an intention of making unlawful gain and for fastening the liability on the Insurance Company.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether respondent No.1 proves that driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and hence respondent No.3 is liable to pay compensation?
7. Thus the issues framed by the Tribunal in both these claim petitions are as below which are identical in nature:
1.
Whether the respective petitioners prove that they sustained injuries in the motor vehicle accident that took place on 29.05.2010 at about 8.30 a.m, on Mysore-Santhemaralli main road near the garden house of petitioner (Shankara)
while negotiating a turn towards his land in his motorcycle, due to rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-10/K-6298 by its rider?
2.
Whether the respective petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. To what order or award?
NC: 2023:KHC:46988
12. The only point that arises for consideration in these appeals are: whether the Tribunal erred in appreciating the evidence on record and in fastening the liability on the owner and rider of the offending motorcycle No.KA-10/K-6298?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, the testimony of RW.2 clearly depict that he was the rider and he did not possess a driving licence.
Therefore, when there is no challenge to the testimony of RW.2, the Tribunal is justified in drawing the conclusion that the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.
Even if we hold that the vehicle owned by respondent No.1 was involved in the accident, the rider of the motorcycle, who was none else than RW.2, was not possessing a valid driving licence and therefore, respondent No.3-Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
When respondent No.1- owner and respondent No.2-Nandeesh have admitted that there was an accident involving the motorcycle belonging to respondent No.1, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on them.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the appeals are devoid of merits.
Hence the following:
ORDER
Both the Appeals are dismissed with costs.
The amount in deposit in both the appeals shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.
